selection: Four measured API requests. One minimal warm-up source-release counterexample is retained separately because it changes the lifecycle conclusion; other warm-up and baseline lifecycles are excluded.
rank_scope: Each P/D engine has its own local TP0/TP1; DCP reuses these two workers. rankS denotes the engine Scheduler.
pairing: Observed get_external_request_id/request_map edges and HTTP child-id convention; no cross-rank left-edge alignment.
warnings: Hooked entry/exit adds Python and I/O overhead; durations are diagnostic, not a performance benchmark.
rankS denotes Scheduler and rankU denotes unknown. Neither is silently relabeled rank0.
A release call is allocator/request bookkeeping; it does not prove immediate physical HBM reuse.
TE sync return >=0 is a host completion observation; absent calls/scopes are not proof of absent transfers.
D _update_waiting_for_remote_kv handles completed receipt; its method boundary alone is not a logged status transition or device decode start.
Requests are joined only by observed local/remote ID or explicit mapping edges; batched calls may belong to several requests.
This MQA DCP2 setup differs from the pull GQA DCP1 setup. Do not use these captures as a pull-versus-push performance comparison.

source_retention_counterexample.interpretation: The P request free call completed before the last observed write returned. The observed Scheduler request-free pathway returned before final write completion. The allocator may defer block-pool return and that branch was not instrumented. No concurrent overwrite or pool reuse was forced, so this does not establish early physical block reuse or a general safety guarantee.
